commit: 07255d10 feat(TW-31): read-time issuer-link trust filter — sanctioned accessor + the structural control that holds it

accessor.trustRule: TRUSTED_MATCH_METHODS = ("cik-exact",) — one member. name-fuzzy excluded (the defect), unlabelled legacy excluded (all 8,334 pre-TW-31 edges), and lei-exact excluded too: exactly ONE lei row exists in identifier_index so that path is unexercised at any scale that would earn trust. Widening the tuple is an operator ruling, pinned by test_lei_exact_is_deliberately_not_trusted.
companions: trusted_issuer_node_id() — one trusted issuer or None (honest absence for the whole legacy cohort, never a fallback to the fuzzy link); raises AmbiguousIssuerLink on two distinct trusted issuers rather than picking one

edge_match_method / trust_state / edge_trust_state / is_trusted — classification helpers (edge_match_method relocated here from issuer_rebuild and re-exported, so its existing importers are unchanged)
accessor.noMutation: Pure read. No mint, no write, no commit, no valid_to closure, no Core update() bypass. A test (test_the_withheld_links_are_still_there_nothing_was_retired) asserts all four seeded edges remain live with valid_to NULL after both a read and a split.

structuralTest.mechanism: AST walk over apps/cockpit/backend/{app,scripts,migrations}/**/*.py (tests/ excluded by the ruling). Two detectors, because there are two ways to read the edge. (1) NAMING it: a string constant containing issued_by as a WORD (catches the bare literal, an f-string fragment, and raw text("... type = 'issued_by'") that an equality check would miss, while not firing on rebuild_issued_by in an __all__), an import of EDGE_TYPE_ISSUED_BY, or any Name/Attribute reference to it. (2) TAKING IT GENERICALLY: a select(Edge) whose enclosing statement constrains no Edge.type, which returns issuer links without ever naming them — the literal walk is blind to those.
structuralTest.allowlistGranularity: (file, enclosing scope), not file. Allowlisting all of resolver.py would leave a hole the size of the module, so the writer is admitted at exactly SecurityResolver.link_security_to_issuer. 9 naming sites allowed: models.py <module> (the definition), issuer_links.py <module>/_scope_clauses/issuer_link_trust_split (the accessor), issuer_rebuild.py <module>/_live_issued_by/rebuild_issued_by (the rebuild routine), resolver.py <module>/SecurityResolver.link_security_to_issuer (the writer). 3 unscoped-reader sites DECLARED: admin_securities.inspect_node (operator-gated raw evidence view that renders each edge's provenance) plus the two accessor functions.
structuralTest.prose: Docstrings and bare doc-comment strings are excluded, and # comments are discarded by the parser, so prose can neither satisfy nor trip the control.
structuralTest.cannotPassVacuously: test_the_allowlist_is_exhaustive_so_the_control_cannot_pass_vacuously asserts the walker found sites at all and that every allowlisted site still exists; the same applies to the unscoped-reader declaration.
structuralTest.limitation: Not claimed as adversary-proof: "issued" + "_by" splicing or a runtime-assembled name would slip past. Aimed at how the defect actually happens (someone writing the obvious query because nothing stopped them), not at deliberate evasion.
structuralTest.testCount: 19 tests in the file (22 test items with parametrisation)

trustStateSplit.http: GET /admin/resolver/issuer-link-trust (operator-gated at the admin_securities router level; query params security_node_id, issuer_node_id, include_closed; pure read)
trustStateSplit.honesty: Every state is a key reporting 0 rather than being omitted, so a consumer sees the split instead of inferring it. unlabelled-legacy is kept separate from name-fuzzy on purpose (label missing vs label admits a guess); collapsing them would report the pre-TW-31 cohort as if it had been assessed. Classification is on the PARSED label, not the SQL substring predicate, so an unknown label lands in unrecognised-label instead of inflating a known bucket by arithmetic. Report also carries total, trusted, untrusted, trusted_match_methods, and distinct issuer/security node counts overall and trusted-only.

remaining: TW-6 must call trusted_issuer_links (or trusted_issuer_node_id) and must render honest absence when it returns nothing. Nothing consumes the accessor yet — this PR builds the boundary and the control, it does not yet have a customer.
Migration 0058 (identifier_index cik domain) is still NOT applied to production, and the rebuild's production dry run is still owed. Both were explicitly out of scope here.

Possible tightening not built, for a ruling: trusted_issuer_links trusts the recorded cik-exact LABEL and does not additionally verify that the target issuer node still claims that CIK in identifier_index. A label-plus-claim agreement check would be strictly stronger; it costs a join and was not in the ruling.

The operator evidence view (GET /admin/nodes/{node_id}) is the one declared generic reader and still returns fuzzy and unlabelled links unfiltered by design. That is now DECLARED and tested (operator-gated, provenance rendered) rather than implicit, but if any non-operator surface ever needs node edges, it must not reuse that shape.
The frontend gate is a text scan with zero current hits; it is not an AST control. A TS reader would be caught, but the check is coarser than the Python one.
notes: Correction to the planner's note in _rd_disclosure_twin/08_build_scope.md (the collapsed-edge resolution section): app/spine/immutability.py enforces append-only on edges at TWO layers, and the primary one is a do_orm_execute statement guard that rejects ORM-issued Core UPDATE/DELETE against the edges table as well as the before_update mapper event. The doc says Core update() is 'intentionally NOT blocked' and that 'closure IS available'; in fact closure is only available inside the allow_atom_backfill contextvar exemption, which only app.securities.backfill_legacy_atoms enters. The real boundary is 'inside the backfill context vs not', not 'Core vs ORM'. This makes the read-time filter more clearly the right option, not less — but the doc's premise for option two is inaccurate.
